title: From Tripods to Bipods Reducing the Queue Number of Planar Graphs Costs Just One Leg

predicted_errors.error_location: Introduction, paragraph ending “inspired a plethora of follow-up works”
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The citation list contains an unresolved placeholder: “[7, 10, 14, 18, ?, 24, 27, 29, 30].” This is not a valid citation and prevents verification of the asserted follow-up work.

predicted_errors.error_location: Claim 3.5, proof in the triangular-face iterative step
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The asserted contradiction is invalid. The proof says that an edge “(u′,v′)” separating a color-1 region must have both endpoints in B_{x_1}, “But then, B_{x_1} is not acyclic.” The existence of one edge whose two endpoints are in B_{x_1} does not create a cycle; an acyclic graph may contain arbitrarily many edges. Moreover, internal triangulation alone does not imply that a color class is separated from all other colors by a single edge rather than by a longer boundary path/cycle. Thus Claim 3.5, on which the triangular iterative construction relies, is not established.

predicted_errors.error_location: Quadrangular-face iterative step, construction of edges e_2 and e_4
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The construction gives inconsistent bag indices: it defines e_2=(v_{k+1},v_2) while stating v_2∈B_{x_3}, then says to connect x_{k+1} to x_2; it defines e_4 with the same endpoint labels and again says to connect to x_2. For a quadrangular face (x_1,x_2,x_3,x_4), e_2 must concern B_{x_2} and e_4 must concern B_{x_4}; otherwise the claimed use of CR2 and the later face decomposition C_{123}/C_{143} do not follow. As written, the insertion rule cannot support the stated invariant.

The path has the wrong number of vertices for the stated BFS layers. The proof chooses d maximally with L_d nonempty, so layers are L_0,...,L_d (d+1 layers), but defines P=(p_1,...,p_d), containing only d vertices. It subsequently needs a path vertex for every layer i∈{0,...,d}, including p_0 or p_{d+1}, neither of which exists. The product embedding proof therefore has an off-by-one domain error.

predicted_errors.error_location: Lemma 4.1 proof, opening induction on n_f
predicted_errors.supporting_evidence: The proof handles n_f=1 and then says “Hence, assume that n_f>2,” leaving the case n_f=2 unproved. In addition, it says it selects a face f “to be drawn next” sharing an edge with an “already drawn subgraph G_f,” but immediately states that G_f is induced by “the first n_f faces”; if f is next, G_f should instead contain the previously drawn faces (normally n_f−1). These gaps make the stated constructive induction incomplete as written.
